title: Trust metadata belongs to the evidence itself, not to the retrieval mechanism
governingInvariant: TRUST METADATA BELONGS TO THE EVIDENCE ITSELF, NOT TO THE RETRIEVAL MECHANISM. Safety must not depend on the model voluntarily calling the right evidence tool.

priorFindingClosed.originalDefect: summarizeContextBundle (semantic/caller.ts) dumped CovenantContextBundle items' raw excerptText verbatim into the model's first turn with zero trust annotation; ToolCallLogEntry.evidenceUnresolved was only ever set inside getDefinition's own tool execution, so a model that answered from the pre-loaded bundle with zero tool calls left toolCallLog empty and both compile.ts and verify.ts had nothing to gate on - reaching COMPLETED / VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND off a genuinely CONFLICTED definition.
priorFindingClosed.disposition: CLOSED - both FALSIFICATION tests in that file were updated (with clear before/after framing preserved) to certify the fixed, fail-closed behavior; all 17 reproduction cases in that file now pass.

trustModel.canonicalEnumReused: amendment/operative-state.ts's DefinitionEvidenceStatus (CURRENT | KNOWN_SUPERSEDED | OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED | AMBIGUOUS_TARGET | PARTIAL_AMENDMENT | HISTORICAL_ONLY) - reused verbatim, never a second parallel vocabulary, per the fix spec's explicit instruction.
trustModel.newPrimitive: resolveOperativeSectionEvidence (amendment/operative-state.ts) - the SECTION-kind sibling of the existing resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence, built by directly reusing OperativeProvisionView fields and getNodeSupersessionStatus rather than any new detection logic. Node-based (accepts an already-resolved {nodeId, sectionRef}) rather than ref-string-based, since every context-retrieval call site already holds a real, uniquely-resolved StructuralNode from its own traversal.
trustModel.newContextItemField: ContextItem.evidenceState?: { status: DefinitionEvidenceStatus; isCurrentTruth: boolean; reason: string } | null - optional (mirrors ToolCallLogEntry.evidenceUnresolved's own established convention) for backward compatibility with pre-existing fixtures/tests; every real context-retrieval call site now populates a real, non-null value for every SECTION/DEFINITION-shaped item.
trustModel.newBundleFields: CovenantContextBundle.hasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence?: boolean and unresolvedEvidenceItemIds?: string[] - computed once in context-retrieval/pipeline.ts's finalize() from the bundle's own items, independent of any tool call.
trustModel.newCompilationResultFields: SemanticCompilationResult.inputHasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence?: boolean and unresolvedEvidenceItemIds?: string[] - copied straight from the context bundle in compile.ts's contextBundleEvidenceFlags(), threaded ALONGSIDE (never instead of) the existing toolCallLog[].evidenceUnresolved mechanism.
trustModel.whyOptionalNotRequired: All new fields were made optional rather than required to avoid a large, risky mechanical rewrite of ~15 pre-existing test files that hand-construct ContextItem/CovenantContextBundle/SemanticCompilationResult object literals. Every REAL production code path (context-retrieval/pipeline.ts, semantic/compile.ts) always populates a real value; undefined is treated identically to 'unresolved-status unknown, never upgraded to a false CURRENT/resolved claim' - the same fail-open-for-genuinely-unchecked-cases discipline EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX already established elsewhere in this codebase.

residualRisk: semantic/tools.ts's getOperativeProvision tool does not set ToolExecutionOutcome.evidenceUnresolved for a genuinely CONFLICTED/AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL section, unlike its getDefinition sibling - a real, pre-existing, POST-tool-call gap (the model DID call a tool) that is a different bug shape than this fix's own pre-tool-call scope. FIX-2's context-bundle-level and defense-in-depth gates independently cover the same underlying scenario for the required end-to-end invariant, so this residual gap does not currently permit VERIFIED/COMPLETED off a CONFLICTED section reached via THIS tool alone reaching a materially different rule than the one already covered - but it should be closed by a future, narrowly-scoped workstream mirroring getDefinition's own fix.

The new trust fields (ContextItem.evidenceState, CovenantContextBundle.hasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence, SemanticCompilationResult.inputHasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence) are optional rather than required, to avoid a large mechanical rewrite of pre-existing test fixtures. This means a FUTURE test or script that hand-constructs one of these object types without populating the new field will silently NOT benefit from the context-bundle-derived gate (though it still benefits from the independent defense-in-depth per-definition re-check in both compile.ts and verify.ts, which requires no bundle cooperation at all). A future hardening pass could tighten these to required once every real and test call site is confirmed migrated.

The defense-in-depth re-check (§5) is scoped to IRDefinition.termName only, not to a defined term referenced only inside an IRRule's own conditions/exceptions/capacityExpression tree (IRDefinedTermReference) - the governing spec named this 'optional but preferred where practical' and the definition-level case is the one the reproduced exploit and required tests exercise; extending it to rule-embedded term references is a reasonable, bounded future addition, not required to close this finding.
